items.title: Health Care Weekly: No Surprises Act Arbiters Dropped for Poor Performance; Hims to Sell Unapproved Wellness Peptides; Telehealth Firm’s GLP-1 Ads Misleading, FDA Says; Novartis Gene Therapies Face Probe over Tumors; Quest Diagnostics Settles Kic - The Capitol Forum
items.reason: The item explicitly addresses No Surprises Act arbiters (IDR entities) being dropped for poor performance, which directly relates to Independent Dispute Resolution process implementation and enforcement of the No Surprises Act.
items.summary: The Capitol Forum reported that No Surprises Act arbiters have been dropped due to poor performance, impacting the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process that handles out-of-network balance-billing disputes. This development affects the operational implementation of the No Surprises Act's core dispute-resolution mechanism and has implications for how healthcare providers and payers resolve payment disagreements. The removal of underperforming IDR entities alters the landscape of which arbiters are available to handle disputes, potentially affecting dispute resolution timelines and outcomes for balance-billing cases. This is relevant to revenue-cycle teams as it directly impacts the IDR process they use to resolve payment disputes with insurers under the No Surprises Act.

items.title: Select Medical alleges Aetna denied 200 of 207 requests for long-term acute care in Pennsylvania - Medical Daily
items.reason: This report describes a provider lawsuit against a major payer (Aetna) alleging systematic claims denials, which directly falls within the payer litigation and enforcement topic covering claims-denial suits.
items.summary: Select Medical has alleged that Aetna denied 200 out of 207 authorization requests for long-term acute care services in Pennsylvania, suggesting a pattern of improper claims denial by the payer. The lawsuit challenges Aetna's denial practices for a specific service line and care setting, raising questions about the insurer's medical necessity determinations and payment obligations. This claim-denial litigation is significant for healthcare revenue-cycle teams as it illustrates ongoing disputes over payer reimbursement decisions and the potential financial impact of high denial rates on provider operations and cash flow.
